lead.hed: The Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group pulled into Singapore for a port visit on its way toward the Middle East
lead.insight: USNI News reported Friday that the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group pulled into Singapore for a port visit, with the strike group expected to head to the Middle East once the visit wraps up. The group includes the carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) with embarked Carrier Air Wing 11, the cruiser USS Chosin (CG-65), and the destroyers USS Paul Hamilton (DDG-60) and USS Decatur (DDG-73). Days before reaching Singapore, a Navy photo posted Nov. 4 showed Theodore Roosevelt conducting a replenishment-at-sea with the Royal Australian Navy oiler HMAS Stalwart while the strike group was underway on routine operations in the 7th Fleet area, in a show of the U.S. Navy's commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo · DVIDS 10069530 · Public domain · USS Theodore Roosevelt conducts a replenishment-at-sea with HMAS Stalwart in the 7th Fleet area, Nov. 4, 2026.

political.hed: Britain and France lead 2,800 troops from 11 nations into Poland Monday to rehearse a postwar Ukraine deployment
political.insight: Defense News reported Saturday that the exercise, KOALICJA 26.2, runs Nov. 9 to 22 across Poland, France, and Turkey under the Coalition of the Willing's military arm, the Multinational Force-Ukraine. American troops will not take part. A British Ministry of Defence statement says the drills combine air, land, and sea forces to test how to move, protect, and supply a force that would help rebuild Ukraine's armed forces once the fighting ends. Belgium, Estonia, Germany, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Turkey, and Britain are also taking part alongside France. Defense News reports U.S., Russian, and Ukrainian negotiators are set to meet in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10 and 11.

political.hed: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected a new warship larger than the country's existing destroyers at Nampho Shipyard
political.insight: USNI News, citing state media reported Wednesday: Kim inspected construction on a warship believed to be a 10,000-ton cruiser-class vessel, larger than North Korea's 5,000-ton destroyers already in service, during a visit to the Nampho Shipyard. The inspection continues a pattern of North Korean leadership attention on the country's surface combatant program.

political.hed: III Marine Expeditionary Force extended a junior-ranks curfew on Okinawa after a Marine was indicted on murder charges
political.insight: USNI News, Friday: III MEF extended the curfew for grades E-1 through E-4 for 30 more days, restricting them to personal housing from midnight to 5 a.m., and kept restrictions on alcohol purchase and consumption for all service members on Okinawa. The curfew had been set to expire Sunday. Japanese prosecutors indicted a Marine lance corporal on murder and robbery charges over the suspected killing of a woman on the island, and the command has not named a new end date for the restrictions.

political.hed: The Army renamed its cooks tactical field feeding specialists to match a battlefield logistics mission
political.insight: Defense News, Friday, citing a late-October ceremony at Fort Lee, Virginia: soldiers in the 92G occupation, formerly culinary specialists, are now tactical field feeding specialists. Quartermaster commandant Col. Stacy Moore-Callaway said the service changed the MOS title not for superficial rebranding but because the character of war has changed, and 92G soldiers who prepare meals now also need to understand battlefield logistics in a contested environment. The Army first formalized the cook position as 94B Food Service Specialist in the 1960s and redesignated it 92G Culinary Specialist in 1995. Stars and Stripes first reported the change.

tech.hed: French sailors ran a close-in defense drill aboard a combat supply ship built to protect itself without an escort
tech.insight: USNI News, Friday, reporting from Toulon: a team of French sailors donned gloves and flash hoods aboard the Batiment ravitailleur de forces-class resupply ship FS Jacques Stosskopf for a close-in defense drill. The ship's short-range combat center and close-in weapon systems have let it operate in the Middle East, including the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the center's commanding officer told reporters aboard the vessel. In 2023, the French Navy was among the first European fleets to provide air defense for merchant vessels transiting the contested strait under Operation Prosperity Guardian.

culture.hed: A Providence essay traces how a 1948 trip to America turned an Egyptian schoolteacher into the godfather of modern jihadism
culture.insight: Providence, Thursday: the essay on Sayyid Qutb recounts how he grew up favoring Western-style education as the path to a better Egypt, admired Hollywood films and liberal ideas, and was sent to study America's school system in 1948 after his writing grew critical of his own government. Arriving in Manhattan that November, his encounter with American life reshaped how he saw both his faith and the West, setting him on the path that produced the ideas behind modern jihadist movements. The piece argues Qutb's turn was less a rejection of modernity than a search for meaning that liberal education, in his account, had failed to supply.

culture.hed: A Law & Liberty review says a new essay collection answers the 1619 Project by recovering the achievement of 1776
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Thursday: reviewer Ilya Shapiro writes that A Nation Born in a Day, edited by American Council of Trustees and Alumni president Michael Poliakoff, gathers nine essays, mostly by historians, that push back on treating the Founding as fraudulent because the men who proclaimed human equality owned slaves. The collection takes direct aim at the New York Times's 1619 Project, arguing the Founding supplied the standard by which later generations judged and corrected injustice rather than a lie to be confessed. Shapiro calls it a substantial contribution to the country's 250th anniversary, crediting Poliakoff's broader work keeping serious liberal education alive against higher education's ideological pressures.
